findings.title: AI tools discovered the PHP vulnerability that could take down 70% of the internet. Now, the race is on to patch it before AI-powered hackers attack
findings.summary_md: Fortune reported the PHP Foundation's emergency disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called php2shell, which allow unauthenticated remote code execution on affected PHP web runtimes. The article says GPT-5.6 Sol and other AI tools helped find the flaws, and that multiple research groups independently found them in August before coordinating fixes with the PHP Foundation. Cloudflare saw tens of thousands of exploit attempts within 45 minutes of reports breaking on Oct. 20, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions by the evening of Oct. 21. AWS said attempts had also appeared before disclosure and that exploitation was broad in the wild.

findings.title: PHP web runtimes (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
findings.summary_md: AWS bulletin 2026-143 says two critical PHP web runtime issues let an unauthenticated remote caller send crafted requests to PHP workers and execute code, read process-accessible data, or cause denial of service. AWS says its own services are not affected, but customers running affected PHP versions in the listed services could be. The issue is bounded to the affected worker and its application-level permissions, with no cross-customer propagation established at publication.

findings.title: AI discovered a software vulnerability that could impact 70% of websites worldwide. The rush is on to patch it
findings.summary_md: PBS reported that governments and companies worked overnight to patch AI-assisted PHP flaws after the FBI's cyber division warned the bugs could allow remote code execution. Officials in Britain, Finland and Japan described limited service disruption, precautionary downtime or instructions for site administrators to install the newly released patch. The FBI recommended taking affected sites offline if operators could not patch immediately.

findings.title: FAA lifts ground stop after more than four hours, but flight cancellations will stretch into the weekend
findings.summary_md: CNBC reported that the FAA halted departures nationwide for more than four hours on Nov. 13 after telecommunications routers were overloaded with data, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy saying they went down. More than 10,000 flights were disrupted; Cirium counted 11,000 scheduled departures after 4 p.m. ET, about 1.5 million passengers and roughly 600 diversions. Homeland Security officials said there was no indication of a cyberattack and that the failure appeared mechanically driven.

findings.title: Microsoft's latest email outage turned into a full blown global cloud crisis
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported that Microsoft's daylong outage began as an Outlook and Teams problem and spread to Copilot, Defender and Intune, with Kentik measuring about 18 hours of downtime. Microsoft said there was no evidence of malicious activity and that the incident was not related to cyber or AI agents, while engineers initially could not identify the cause. The company did not answer questions about whether it had the logs needed to detect malicious activity.

findings.title: Microsoft reveals that an old bug caused the massive outage that took its services offline
findings.summary_md: Engadget summarized Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report, which identified three root causes: a Teams gateway failure that overloaded the primary gateway, roughly 14 percent of that gateway's capacity already out of service, and a latent bug dating to July. The combination caused a traffic backlog and server failure during peak US afternoon hours, and a rollback was not possible. Microsoft said a final report would follow later that week.

findings.title: Exclusive: Highly classified US national security communications network goes down, sources say
findings.summary_md: CNN reported that NSANet went offline on Nov. 17, with the NSA calling it temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance and sources saying there was no evidence of a cyberattack. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox Business that the outage came from applying a patch for major software vulnerabilities discovered the previous month, and CNN identified those flaws as PHP issues that AI tools helped researchers exploit. Staff at Fort Meade moved from code yellow to code green and back to code orange as restoration continued.
